narrative:
The model estimated a 40% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. This is a risk estimate, not a certainty of default. For this loan product, that estimated risk was above the bank’s approval threshold, so the application was denied.

The strongest factor was your checking account status. Your account is overdrawn (below 0 DM). Only about 12.6% of approved applicants had this status, while most had no overdraft, so this pushed the prediction toward bad credit more than anything else. The second most influential factor was the share of monthly disposable income needed for repayments. At 2%, it is below the approved-applicant average of about 3%, and this worked in your favor, lowering the estimated risk. The third factor was savings. Your savings are below 100 DM. This is fairly common—about 45.6% of approved applicants are in that range—but it still nudged the prediction toward bad credit because a larger savings buffer would be more reassuring.

The most useful next step is to bring your checking account back into credit and keep it there for several months. Build savings above 100 DM if possible, avoid new credit, and provide recent statements showing a stable balance. You can also ask the bank what cutoff applied and whether a smaller or differently structured loan would be considered.
